Goldman Sachs Interview Experience (Internship) 
Atharva Thorve | T.Y. B.Tech IT 2018-22 
 
 
 
 
Aptitude Test (100+ participants) 
27th August 2020 
The test was conducted on Hackerrank. It included multiple sections. Each section had 
a corresponding timer. You cannot submit answers to any questions of that section if its 
timer runs out. You can attempt the sections themselves in any order. 
 
Section 1 (30 mins) 
 
1. In the first question, we are provided with an array of points (i and j) values and 
we had to find the sum of the pairwise distance between all of the points. The 
distance formula was provided and it was |Xi - Yi| + |Xj - Yj|. This question was 
clearly meant to be solved in O(n​2​) time so I implemented that solution and it 
passed 11/12 test cases. After observing the failed test case I realized I had to 
calculate modulo of the answer with either 10​9​ + 7 or 10​9​ + 9. So I tried the first 
value and it passed so I did not check it with the other value. 
 
2. We have coordinates of the starting and destination points in a 2D plane. We also 
have a list of pairs of points where each pair represents a straight line that 
passes through that pair of points. The task was to find the minimum euclidean 
distance of the path from start to destination point without crossing over any of 
the lines. However, you can pass through the endpoints of the line. For example, 
The starting point is (0,0) destination point is (3,0) and there is a line passing 
through (1,0) and (2,1) so the shortest path would (0,0) -> (1,0) -> (3,0) with 
distance 3. I was able to pass 4 out of the 12 test cases. 
 
Section 2 (~20mins)

10 math MCQs. +5, -2 marking scheme. 
Questions were based on probability, trigonometry, geometry, PnC, and number 
theory. I attempted questions from probability and PnC. The questions are really 
difficult and the time limit is very low so don’t waste much time on one question. 
 
Section 3 (~15 mins) 
 
7 CS subjects’ based MCQs. +5, -2 marking scheme 
Questions were from OS, DBMS, Computer Networking, Computer Architecture, 
Data Structures, and Algorithms. 
This section was fairly simple compared to the previous section but the time limit was 
also very low for this part. If you practice these concepts then the section will feel easy. 
 
Section 4 (45 mins) 
 
This section consisted of only one question but it was a long one. 
We were given an MxN matrix consisting of numbers from 1 to F where each 
number represents a different type of flower. We had to print the number of cells 
in the largest connected component of the graph with at most 2 different types of 
flowers in it. You can move in any of the 4 perpendicular directions from a cell. 
You can start from any cell as well. It took me around 38 minutes and multiple tries but 
I was able to solve this question completely.  
Hint: I used bfs but also added some optimization:) 
 
Section 5 (15 mins) 
 
1. Write about a project that shows your passion. 
 
2. How will you handle a situation wherein you’re facing a deadline and your team 
member won’t be to work due to some emergency?

These questions don’t hold much importance compared to others but still think about 
them and try to answer as honestly as possible. 
One thing you can do is use the Grammarly extension which comes in handy for any 
section like this ;) 
 
The list of candidates came in on 1st Sept and the interviews were held on 2nd so start 
prepping for the interviews beforehand. 29 candidates were shortlisted for the interview 
rounds. (All interview rounds were conducted on the same day). 
 
 
 
Interview Round 1 - (Technical) (~30 mins) 
 
The questions of this round varied from interviewer to interviewer. Some candidates 
were asked about their projects, or system design or CS subjects. The coding was done 
over Hackerrank Codepair. The interview rounds took place on Zoom. 
 
To be honest my interviewer was really chill guy so the experience was really 
anti-climactic but still it was really fun. 
I was asked to introduce myself. In this question try to highlight your achievements as 
much as possible but don’t make it too long. My suggestion will be that you prepare 
something from the start like a few points and then use them. 
Then I was asked about my resume so I just went through it and explained my skills, 
projects, and certificates. They grill you on the projects section so be prepared for it. 
After this, I was asked to log into Codepair. I was asked only one question 
 
1. To find the second maximum in an array​. 
 
This is it, I was asked only one question which is very simple. 
But ​make sure you don’t mess up a question like this as the interviewer knows this 
question is very simple so expects an accurate answer. Always think about the edge cases 
in these questions as the interviewer will try to trip you up.

After this, the interviewer asked me about myself other than technical stuff. 
The interviewer asked if I had any questions. ​Always ​ask a question, you can learn a lot 
from the interviewer’s experience. Keep at least one question prepared and since it was a 
technical interview ask technical questions instead of HR questions. 
 
16​ candidates were shortlisted for Round 2. 
 
 
 
Interview Round 2 - (Technical) (~45 mins) 
 
The interviewer asked me to introduce myself. Then he asked to log in to Codepair 
again. 
 
I was asked only one question: 
 
1. Given an array of songs implement the shuffle feature such that each song which 
hasn’t been played yet has an ​equal​ probability of getting selected and songs 
which were already selected had ​zero​ probability. 
So at first, I inquired if I could use an ​ArrayList​ (similar to vector in c++) so he said 
yes. 
Since the question required usage of the ​Random​ module but since I had not used the 
module much he told me what methods I could use from it. 
 
So after all this, I solved the question using an ​ArrayList​. So he modified the question 
and told me if I could solve it if I was given an ​array ​instead of an ​ArrayList ​and also 
without using any extra space. I thought about it for some time and came up with a 
solution that was satisfying all the constraints and was optimized.  
 
Then he asked me a system design question 
In which we had to design a system to sell apples. So I went on to designing the database 
schema but he stopped me midway and said he was looking for like what technologies I 
would use for frontend, middleware, and database. Then after answering these

questions I was asked questions related to NoSQL and SQL databases and when to use 
which. 
 
Then he asked me how will I implement the feature where changes made by one user 
were reflected to another user in realtime. I suggested the answer WebSockets from 
which he was satisfied but was still looking for something better. Sadly he never revealed 
the answer he was looking for :( 
 
Finally, he asked me if I had any questions. Again I’ll emphasis that do ask a question 
this shows to the interviewer you are proactively researching things and are actually very 
interested. 
 
7​ candidates were shortlisted for Round 3. 
 
 
 
Interview Round 3 (HR) (~20 mins) 
 
My third round was technically was not a round for selection as at the end they revealed 
that they had already selected me and this round was just for fun. 
But ​still here are the details :) 
 
There were 10 people in the round including me. There were 6 devs, 1 person from 
HR, and 2 two of my classmates who were also selected. 
They just asked some typical HR questions like: 
 
1. Why should Goldman Sachs hire you guys? 
 
Then the interviewers just went on asking some moral questions which were not that 
relevant but we had no idea that time so we tried to answer them as honestly as possible. 
 
And that is it​.

At the end total of ​6​ candidates were selected. 
 
 
 
Preparation: 
 
1. Start preparing for interview questions as early on as possible. 
 
2. There are multiple coding platforms for practice but here is a list that might be 
very useful: 
a. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/practice-for-cracking-any-coding-intervie
w/ 
b. https://leetcode.com/problemset/top-interview-questions/ 
c. https://www.interviewbit.com/courses/programming/ 
 
3. Read interview experiences for all the companies. That will give you a good feel 
of how interviews are conducted. The exact format may change but you’ll notice 
a pattern in them. 
 
4. Do prepare for puzzles from geeksforgeeks. 
 
5. Focus on ​CS ​subjects like OS, DBMS, and DSA as many questions are asked 
related to this. 
 
 
 
Advice 
 
1. Practice ​HR-related ​questions as they are nearly equally important. 
 
2. Always be ​confident ​of what the answer you give as the interviewer tries to grill 
you as much as possible.

3. Research​ the company and prepare a list of questions that you can ask them. 
 
4. Almost always there are delays in the procedure so ​be patient​. 
 
5. Do not study or keep anything for the day of the interview. 
 
Since my interviews were a bit simpler and anti-climactic this doesn’t mean all are, so be 
well prepared for any situation. 
 
 
 
All the Best
